verdicts.handler_address: 0x1854 (lua_duaLogoutInfoGet in lib/lua/5.1/captivePortalLib.so); Lua chain: var/www/platform.lua -> var/www/duaLogout.lua -> duaCP.logout -> duaCP.parse_logoutInfo -> captivePortalLib.duaLogoutInfoGet

sink (arm-linux-gnueabi-objdump -d lib/lua/5.1/captivePortalLib.so): 1854 <lua_duaLogoutInfoGet> sub sp,sp,#948; 18f4 bl lua_tolstring (arg idx 1 = extCpResult); 1900 bl strcpy with dst r4=sp+0x0c (memset'd 512 bytes at 18c4) -- unbounded copy of full attacker string; 190c bl duaServerResponsePrase (splits "key":"value" pairs); 1984 bl strcmp(key,"clientMac") / 1998 bl strcmp(key,"clientIp"); 1960 bl strcpy dst r9=sp+0x37e (50-byte buffer); 19b8 bl strcpy dst sp+0x34c (50-byte buffer)
key strings: objdump -s -j .rodata 0x3168 -> 'clientMac', 0x3174 -> 'clientIp' (the two strcmp match keys feeding the 0x1960/0x19b8 strcpy sinks)

offset cross-check with public exploit (github.com/DelspoN/CVE-2024-57376): payload = 86*'a' + ROP inside {"clientMac":"..."}; 0x37e (clientMac buf) + 86 (0x56) = 0x3d4 = saved LR slot of lua_duaLogoutInfoGet frame (push 9 regs + sub sp,#948) -- exact match, proving the 0x1960 strcpy is the exploited overflow
no patch trace: this 3.17B901C build (2022-06-10) is the final firmware (D-Link advisory: EOL/EOS, no fixed firmware ever released); no length checks added around any strcpy in lua_duaLogoutInfoGet

companion-process check (4.e): not applicable/none -- sink is in-process: bin/cgi (Kepler cgilua) dlopens /pfrm2.0/lib/lua/5.1/captivePortalLib.so directly (exploit memory map confirms the .so mapped inside the cgi process); parameters are not forwarded via IPC/pipe/shared file to any companion daemon before the sink
verdicts.reason: Version gate passes exactly (3.17B901C = inclusive upper bound of affected range), and the full pre-auth chain exists in this rootfs: POST /platform.cgi action=duaLogout&externalCpResult=... -> platform.lua pre-auth whitelist (DUA_LOGOUT_PAGE) -> duaLogout.lua -> duaCP.logout -> parse_logoutInfo -> captivePortalLib.duaLogoutInfoGet @0x1854, where lua_tolstring'd attacker string is strcpy'd (0x1900/0x1960/0x19b8) into 512B/50B/50B stack buffers with no bounds check; 86-byte overflow offset to saved LR matches the public exploit.
